name: Honeycombe-on-the-Wold
tagline: A honey-stone village in a green fold of the Wolds.

projects.name: Sweep the Station Lane
projects.desc: Clear the lane from the Halt so visitors can find the High Street.

projects.name: Repaint the Waiting Shelter
projects.desc: Chocolate and cream, just as the Great Western intended. And polish that window!

projects.name: Station Flowers
projects.desc: Hanging baskets under the canopy and a flower tub by the line. Mr Figg has entered 'Best-Kept Station' too.

projects.name: Mend the Green's Gate
projects.desc: The old kissing gate onto the Green has been stuck since the Coronation.

projects.name: Repaint Kiosk & Pillar Box
projects.desc: Post Office red, two coats. Mrs Pemberton will inspect personally.

projects.name: Bunting on the High Street
projects.desc: Flags from bracket to bracket, a window box for the Post Office and a basket by the tea room.

projects.name: Clear the Riverside Path
projects.desc: Brambles have swallowed the footpath down to Weavers' Row.

projects.name: Varnish Benches, Scrub the Cross
projects.desc: The Market Cross hasn't been scrubbed since 1911. The Colonel has strong feelings.

projects.name: A Duck House for the Pond
projects.desc: A proper house for the ducks, a bird bath and bunting round the Green.

projects.name: Free the Mill Race
projects.desc: Clear the weed from the mill race so the old wheel can turn again.

projects.name: Paint the Weavers' Doors
projects.desc: A fresh coat for the doors of the Row and window boxes all along.

projects.name: Bunting along the Row
projects.desc: Flags along the cottages and a flower trough by the bridge.

projects.name: Clear the Brambles on Pub Lane
projects.desc: Mabel says half her regulars got lost in the brambles last winter.

projects.name: Paint the Mill Doors
projects.desc: Mill-green paint for the mill door and the stable door opposite.

projects.name: The Miller's Garden
projects.desc: A bench by the ford, a beehive on the bank and a trough of flowers.

projects.name: Oil the Lychgate
projects.desc: The lychgate squeals like a bagpipe. The Reverend would like it to stop.

projects.name: Strip & Varnish the Pub Door
projects.desc: Oak should look like oak. And the garden gate needs doing while we're at it.

projects.name: Festoon Lights for the Garden
projects.desc: Strings of lights along the eaves, baskets by the door and a bird bath on the lawn.

projects.name: Prune the Rose Arch
projects.desc: Nan Honeysett's gate is lost somewhere behind her roses.

projects.name: Regild the Church Clock
projects.desc: Gold leaf for the clock face and a coat of varnish for the church door.

projects.name: Churchyard Flowers
projects.desc: A bench for weary bell-ringers and flowers along the path.

projects.name: Freshen the Hives
projects.desc: A lick of white paint for the hives and a scrub for the greenhouse.

projects.name: Fête Day at Rose Cottage
projects.desc: Bunting, a bird bath and a picnic hamper. The judges are coming for tea.

intro.title: A new assignment
intro.body:
Dear Photographer,

Welcome to the Wold & Vale Postcard Company! Your first assignment is Honeycombe-on-the-Wold, which has entered the county's Best-Kept Village competition.

The village is lovely, but it has let itself go a little. Tidy each spot until it is picture-perfect, then take the postcard. They sell like hot cakes at the Post Office, and every penny goes to the village restoration fund.

The train gets in at eleven. Colonel Whitby will meet you.

Yours, with great expectations,
Clementine Ashby
Editor

welcome.title: Welcome to Honeycombe!
welcome.body:
Ah, the photographer! Capital. Colonel Whitby, chair of the Best-Kept Village Committee.

The judges arrive in the spring and, between ourselves, the place is a shambles. Litter on the platform, signs all anyhow.

Start here at the Halt, would you? Tidy up, take your snap. Then we'll talk about the High Street.

teaser.title: A postcard from Cornwall
teaser.body:
Letter for you, sorry it's late. Postmark says Porthkennack Cove. Picture of a harbour on the front. Lovely, isn't it?

Someone there's heard about your postcards, I reckon.

finale.title: Your next assignment
finale.body:
Dear Photographer,

Best-Kept Village! The whole company is thrilled, and the Honeycombe postcards are our best-sellers of the year.

Which brings me to Porthkennack Cove in Cornwall. A fishing village on a harbour, with storms, sea mist and gulls with opinions. They've entered the Coastal Village Prize and they're asking for you by name.

The sleeper leaves Paddington on Friday. Say the word and I'll book your ticket.

Yours, very proudly,
Clementine Ashby
